The diffusion horizon for open-weight models to reach equivalent capability to commercial frontier models is estimated at approximately three months.

factual_claims.claim: The architecture uses SLH-DSA for long-term root signing to protect against future quantum-computing threats, specifically the 'harvest-now, forge-later' attack vector. This hash-based signature scheme is chosen because its security relies on preimage resistance rather than the lattice-based hardness assumptions that might be vulnerable to future fault-tolerant quantum computers.
The verification cost for the proposed cryptographic release architecture is approximately one to two milliseconds on commodity hardware.
